headline: Executive order further extends the federal government's delay in enforcing the law that restricts TikTok in the United States.
what_it_does: This order extends, again, an earlier pause on enforcing a federal law aimed at TikTok. That law generally bars app stores and web hosting companies from supporting TikTok unless its China-based owner sells it. The title and the lack of a summary do not give the new end date or other details.

who_it_affects.group: People in the US who use TikTok
who_it_affects.how: The app can keep operating while enforcement of the law stays on hold.

who_it_affects.group: App stores and internet hosting companies
who_it_affects.how: They get more time before the government enforces the law's penalties for supporting TikTok.

who_it_affects.group: TikTok and its parent company, ByteDance
who_it_affects.how: They get more time to work out a possible sale or other arrangement before the law is enforced.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses and creators who earn money on TikTok
who_it_affects.how: They can keep using the platform during the extended delay.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed June 19, 2025; the length of the extension is not stated in the provided material.
